title: Role-based access, vendor onboarding, and spend workflows — Playbook
author: Ava Martinez
content:
Overview

This playbook defines the end-to-end operational patterns that tie together: role-based access control (RBAC), change management for identity and permissions, data stewardship, procurement & expense approvals, vendor onboarding, and travel/expense templates. It is intended for requesters, managers, IT Security, Finance, Procurement, Data Stewards, and People Ops. The goal is predictable, auditable, and least-privilege-aligned decisions for any access, spend, or vendor request.

Scope

- Applies to all full-time employees, contractors, and third-party vendors who require systems access, vendor contracts, or reimbursable travel.
- Covers SSO groups, cloud account roles, privileged access, software procurement, vendor onboarding, and expense reimbursement.
- Does NOT replace product-specific onboarding docs; it defines the company-wide lifecycle and templates.

Key principles

1) Least privilege by default. Grant the minimum role necessary for 14 days for trial requests unless manager explicitly justifies longer duration.
2) Separation of duties. Approvals for spend and access must come from different approvers when value or privilege exceeds thresholds below.
3) Auditability. Every request must have a linked ticket and an approver chain recorded in the governance system.
4) Data-aware decisions. Data classification (Public/Internal/Restricted/PII) determines additional approvals and vendor requirements.

Roles and responsibilities

- Requester: Submits access, vendor, or expense request using the relevant template and attaches justification and duration.
- Manager (approver 1): Confirms business need and recommended role/limit.
- Access Approver / IT Security (approver 2 for high-privilege requests): Reviews technical scope and approves role, MFA, and session policies.
- Finance / Procurement (spend approver): Approves purchases, PO issuance, and contract terms for vendor spend.
- Data Steward: Confirms whether data involved is restricted or PII and sets data protection controls.
- People Ops: Ensures contractor/vendor onboarding steps (IDs, background checks) are complete.

Access request lifecycle (RBAC + change mgmt)

1) Request initiation
   - Use the "Access Request" template (link: /confluence/templates/access-request). Required fields: requester, manager, system, role, justification, duration, business impact, data classification.
2) Manager approval (within 48 hours for standard requests).
3) Security review (required for: privileged roles, access to Restricted/PII data, or cross-account/cloud access). Security review targets: 24 hours SLT for urgent, 72 hours for routine.
4) Provisioning & evidence capture
   - Provisioning teams create ticket in ITSM and attach the request.
   - Log entry added to the Access Registry: | Date | User | Role | System | Duration | Approvers | Ticket |. Example row: | 2027-10-12 | jane.doe@redwood.com | db-reader | analytics-db | 30d | manager/itsec | IT-45312 |
5) Expiration and review
   - Automated expiration via SSO group lifecycle where supported. Expirations at 14/30/90/365 days depending on role.
   - Quarterly entitlement reviews for privileged roles.

Approval thresholds and escalation matrix

- Low risk (value < $5k, non-privileged access): Manager approval only.
- Medium risk (value $5k–$50k, access to Internal data): Manager + Finance/Procurement.
- High risk (value > $50k, access to Restricted/PII or privileged system): Manager + IT Security + Finance + Data Steward.
- Emergency access: Manager + IT Security by pager; emergency access must be time-boxed to < 8 hours and followed by post-facto audit.

Vendor onboarding and contract workflow

1) Supplier pre-check (Procurement): Verify supplier in vendor registry. If new, initiate Vendor Intake Form (link: /confluence/templates/vendor-intake).
2) Risk scoping (Security & Legal): Determine required controls based on data class, including encryption, SOC 2, or custom controls for Restricted data.
3) Commercial negotiation (Procurement/Finance): Sign-offs required based on thresholds above. Attach PO where applicable.
4) Technical onboarding (IT/People Ops): Create access, service accounts, and place vendor accounts into "vendor" SSO groups with limited privileges.
5) Contract & renewal cadence: Vendor contracts must include security addendum for any vendor with access to Restricted/PII and be scheduled for renewal reviews 60 days before end-of-term.

Vendor risk controls (checklist)

- Does the vendor process Restricted or PII data? (Y/N)
- Required attestations: SOC 2 Type II / ISO 27001 / GDPR DPA (where applicable)
- Network restrictions: Dedicated VPC peering or IP allowlist required?
- Encryption: Data-at-rest and in-transit required for Restricted data
- Right to audit clause included?

Procurement & expense workflow (step-by-step)

1) Requisition: Requester creates requisition with cost center, GL code, business justification, and vendor ID (if known).
2) Manager approval: Confirms need and budget.
3) Finance review: Verifies budget and issues PO as required.
4) Receipt & invoice matching: Accounts Payable matches invoice to PO and closure.
5) Expense reimbursement: Employee follows Travel & Expense template (link: /confluence/templates/travel-expense). Receipts > $75 require itemized receipts.

Travel policy highlights

- Booking: Employees should use approved travel portal (Concur) and select economy fares unless exception is approved 72 hours prior.
- Per diem: Domestic meals capped at $75/day; international rates follow country-specific matrix (link: /confluence/policies-and-process/international-travel-matrix).
- Approvals: Manager + People Ops for international travel to Restricted/High-risk regions.
- Corporate card use: Corporate card may be used for approved travel and vendor charges; reconcile within 15 calendar days.

Data classification & controls

- Public: No controls beyond standard access.
- Internal: Default classification for internal business info; follow RBAC controls.
- Restricted: Requires Data Steward review, encryption, vendor controls, and additional monitoring.
- PII: Has specific handling procedures; must be logged and access strictly limited.

Templates (quick reference)

- Access Request subject line: "Access Request — [System] — [User] — [Duration]"
- Vendor Intake: Minimal required fields: Legal Name, Tax ID, Country, Data Types Processed, Primary Contact, Security Certifications.
- PO requisition headline: "Requisition: [Vendor] — [Business Unit] — Estimated spend $[amount]"
- Travel expense email: "T&E Claim — [Employee] — [MM/YYYY]"

Operational SLAs and monitoring

- Standard access request: acknowledge within 4 business hours, complete within 48 business hours.
- Privileged access request: acknowledge within 1 business hour, complete within 24 business hours.
- Vendor intakes: initial procurement screener response within 2 business days.
- Expense reimbursements: processed within 15 business days of receipt submission.

Auditing and evidence retention

- All approvals, tickets, and contract documents must be retained for 7 years for audit and compliance.
- Access Registry exports are performed monthly and stored in the secure evidence bucket (S3 path: s3://redwood-compliance/access-exports/).

Change management for permissions and systems

- Minor changes (role mapping, group membership): documented in ITSM and deployed within maintenance window.
- Major changes (new identity provider integration, cross-account role creation): require Change Advisory Board (CAB) review, test plan, backout plan, and runbook. CAB meets weekly for non-emergency changes.

Escalation & incident playbacks

- Unauthorized access detected: Notify IT Security and the access approver within 1 hour. Initiate emergency de-provision and forensic snapshot.
- Vendor breach: Follow Incident Response — Vendor playbook and notify Legal & Procurement within 1 hour of detection.

Templates and sample artifacts (links)

- /confluence/templates/access-request
- /confluence/templates/vendor-intake
- /confluence/templates/travel-expense
- /confluence/eng-infra/identity-runbook (for onboarding service accounts)

Change log and governance

- Policy owner: People Ops (primary) with Security and Finance as co-owners.
- Review cadence: Annual review or sooner if regulatory change.
- Change requests for this playbook: file via the Governance Requests space (link: /confluence/policies-and-process/playbook-change-requests).

Appendix A — Quick checklists

Access request checklist (requester):
- [ ] Manager name and email provided
- [ ] Business justification included
- [ ] Duration and expiry date specified
- [ ] Data classification enumerated

Vendor onboarding checklist (procurement):
- [ ] Vendor Intake Form completed
- [ ] Security certifications verified
- [ ] Contract includes security addendum for Restricted/PII
- [ ] PO and payment terms agreed

Expense checklist (employee):
- [ ] Itemized receipts attached for all expenses > $75
- [ ] Travel approval attached for international travel
- [ ] Cost center and GL code provided

Contact matrix

- People Ops (policy owner): people-ops@redwood.com
- IT Security (access escalation): it-security@redwood.com
- Procurement: procurement@redwood.com
- Finance / AP: ap@redwood.com

End of document.
